“Katotohanan at Pananagutan”—this was the demand of Akbayan Partylist, Tindig Pilipinas, and Youth Against Kurakot (YAK!) as they held a White Ribboning and Noise Barrage at Kamias cor. EDSA on Friday morning, calling for the immediate filing of charges and imprisonment of those implicated in the trillion-peso flood control scandal. The groups distributed and pinned white ribbons on pedestrians and commuters to symbolize the people’s demand for truth, justice, and accountability.

Youth Against Kurakot Lead Convenor and Akbayan Youth Secretary General Khylla Meneses expressed frustration over the government’s slow response to the corruption issue, “The Filipino people work hard, but the corrupt steal harder. Kaya ang panawagan natin ay sana naman sipagan pa ng gobyerno ang pagiimbestiga, pag-file ng kaso, at pagpapakulong sa lahat ng mga kurakot,” Meneses said.

“Anong petsa na? Magta-tatlong buwan na ang lumipas pagkatapos ng SONA ni Marcos Jr. at ipinangako niya na papanagutin ang mga kurap. Ilang baha pa ba ang hihintayin? Ilang bagyo pa ba ang papadaanin? Babad na babad na kami dito sa baha oh,” she added.

Read more: https://t.co/cWMx7S1OZl

NOW: Students from various UP Manila colleges walked out of their classes and blocked Pedro Gil St. cor. Taft Ave. to protest widespread corruption under the Marcos-Duterte regime.

Following successful walkout on Sept. 12, where over 600 students marched, today’s mobilization carries calls against budget cuts in UP Manila and the Philippine General Hospital, reflected in long-standing infrastructure delays across campus grounds.

Participants will later join other universities in a march to Mendiola, where the program for the National Day of Action Kontra Korapsyon will commence.
